title: Common quotient reduction of the geometric scalar comparison
statement:
Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism of small-site topoi, with $u^{-1}$ left exact and left adjoint to $u_*$. Let $R\to B$ and $R'\to B'$ be flat morphisms of commutative ring sheaves. Give an identification $u^{-1}R\cong R'$ and a compatible map $u^{-1}B\to B'$. Let $J_n\subset R$ and $J_n'\subset R'$ be decreasing ideal sheaves such that the latter is generated by the image of $u^{-1}J_n$. Assume the induced maps identify $S_n=R/J_n=B/J_nB$ and $S_n'=R'/J_n'=B'/J_n'B'$, compatibly with transitions. In the unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], use K-flat ringed pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For every $M\in D(B)$ the scalar-insertion comparison
$$Lu_R^*\operatorname{Res}M\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}'Lu_B^*M$$
has an invertible finite reduction. Its inverse is the canonical $S_n'$-linear isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Res}'Lu_B^*M\otimes_{R'}^L S_n'\cong Lu_R^*(\operatorname{Res}M\otimes_R^L S_n).$$
For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$, insertion is induced by $r'\otimes p\mapsto\bar r'\otimes p$ from $R'\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}P$ to $\operatorname{Res}'(B'\otimes_{u^{-1}B}u^{-1}P)$, where $\bar r'$ is the image of $r'$ under $R'\to B'$ (so $1\otimes p\mapsto1\otimes p$). The isomorphisms are natural in $M$, compatible with quotient transitions and quotient units, and coherent for identity and composable geometric morphisms with such data under the canonical pullback compositors. Tensor and pure sections are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]; K-flatness and flatness are [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

proof.text: Choose a complex representing $M$ and a quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat $B$-complex $P$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-scalar-restriction-kflat], $\operatorname{Res}P$ is K-flat with flat $R$-terms, using the assumed flatness of $R\to B$. Restriction itself is exact: it keeps the underlying abelian sheaf and each module kernel and cokernel, with the scalar action restricted through the ring map [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Thus $\operatorname{Res}M$ is represented by $\operatorname{Res}P$. All subsequent constructions use this single $P$, for every $n$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YN (definition-K-flat); flat scalar restriction as in the proof of Tag 06YY

proof.text: Put $A=u^{-1}B$ and $Q=u^{-1}P$, retaining the transported $A$-action on $Q$. Exactness of algebraic inverse image [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact] identifies $u^{-1}(R/J_n)$ with $R'/J_n'=S_n'$: apply it to the cokernel of $J_n\to R$, whose image ideal is $J_n'$ by hypothesis. For $B$, let $J_nB\subset B$ be the ideal sheaf of local finite sums $\sum_i j_ib_i$; the sum-of-products map $\coprod_{k\geq1}(J_n\times B)^k\to J_nB$ is an epimorphism of sheaves. Since $u^{-1}$ preserves finite products (so commutes with the ring operations) and, as a left adjoint, coproducts and epimorphisms, and since it preserves the monomorphism $J_nB\subset B$ by the cited exactness, $u^{-1}(J_nB)\subset A$ is the image of $\coprod_k(u^{-1}J_n\times A)^k\to A$, i.e. the ideal of local sums $\sum_ij_ia_i$ with $j_i$ in the image $J_n'$ of $u^{-1}J_n$; thus $u^{-1}(J_nB)=J_n'A$. Cokernel preservation now gives $A/J_n'A\cong u^{-1}(B/J_nB)\cong u^{-1}(R/J_n)\cong S_n'$ as ring sheaves. This isomorphism is the map induced by $A\to B'\to B'/J_n'B'=S_n'$: both are $R'$-algebra maps out of $A/J_n'A$, to which $R'$ surjects, so they agree; the same holds for the transitions. Inverse image of scalar multiplication identifies the underlying $R'$-complex of $Q$ with $u^{-1}\operatorname{Res}P$. Since the coefficient map $u^{-1}R\cong R'$ is an isomorphism, $u_R^*$ is this exact inverse-image functor. It therefore preserves quasi-isomorphisms and computes $Lu_R^*$ on every complex, including a quotient complex which need not be K-flat.

Let $F=B'\otimes_A Q=u_B^*P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], $F$ is K-flat over $B'$ with flat terms, without any flatness assumption on $A\to B'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], it represents $Lu_B^*M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-scalar-restriction-kflat], using the separate assumed flatness of $R'\to B'$, $\operatorname{Res}'F$ is K-flat with flat $R'$-terms and represents $\operatorname{Res}'Lu_B^*M$.

On the models just obtained, define $\alpha_P:u_R^*\operatorname{Res}P\to\operatorname{Res}'F$ by $r'\otimes q\mapsto\overline{r'}\otimes q$. The tensor balancing relation is respected because the square of structural ring maps commutes. Bilinearity and the sheaf tensor universal property give an $R'$-linear map; it commutes with differentials since neither coefficient has nonzero degree. The scalar-extension adjunction unit is $q\mapsto1\otimes q$ by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus], so this is precisely the scalar-insertion comparison, with the prescribed normalization. It is natural on complexes. The computations of derived pullback above and the localization equivalence on flat-term K-flat complexes [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] descend it to the claimed comparison on $D(B)$.

proof.text: Write $S=S_n'$. The source finite reduction is represented by $U_n=S\otimes_{R'}u^{-1}\operatorname{Res}P$: the unreduced source is K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], and K-flat scalar extension computes derived reduction by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Also $\operatorname{Res}M\otimes_R^L S_n$ is represented by $S_n\otimes_R\operatorname{Res}P$. Apply the exact $u_R^*$ of step 2. The normalized ordinary tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison-construction, def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison] identifies its image with $U_n$, with local inverse-image pure generators sent to the corresponding pure generators. Thus $U_n$ represents the right side of the asserted isomorphism, with its actual $S$-action.

By step 3 and K-flat derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the target finite reduction is represented by $V_n=S\otimes_{R'}\operatorname{Res}'F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-common-quotient-reduction-tower] to $R'\to B'$ and $F$, using exactly $R'/J_n'=B'/J_n'B'=S$. The ordinary comparison on this single flat-term K-flat model identifies $V_n$ with $S\otimes_{B'}F$, both through the sheaf quotient $F/J_n'F$; it sends $s\otimes f$ to $s\otimes f$ and $1\otimes f$ to $1\otimes f$. Thus it preserves the given $S$-action and the quotient-unit normalization, rather than merely giving an abstract derived isomorphism. There is a further ordinary chain isomorphism
$$S\otimes_{B'}(B'\otimes_AQ)\longrightarrow S\otimes_AQ,\qquad s\otimes(b'\otimes q)\longmapsto s\,\overline{b'}\otimes q.$$
Its inverse sends $s\otimes q$ to $s\otimes(1\otimes q)$. The two balanced tensor relations show these maps are well-defined and inverse. These are maps of sheaf tensors by their universal property, and their formulas commute with differentials.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), balanced tensor universal property; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor)

proof.text: The ordinary map $h_n:U_n=S\otimes_{R'}\operatorname{Res}_{R'}Q\to S\otimes_AQ$ sends $s\otimes q$ to $s\otimes q$. It is invertible because $A/J_n'A=S=R'/J_n'$. Explicitly $U_n$ is $Q/J_n'Q$: $1\otimes q\leftrightarrow[q]$, and $s\otimes q\mapsto s[q]$, with local lifts of $s$ to $R'$ independent modulo $J_n'$. The $A$-action on this quotient factors through $A/J_n'A=S$; hence this same formula is balanced over $A$ and defines the inverse of $h_n$. This argument is applied degreewise and sheafifies, so proves an $S$-linear chain isomorphism without assuming any surjectivity on sections of a quotient sheaf. Under steps 5 and 6 the reduced $\alpha_P$ is $s\otimes q\mapsto s\otimes(1\otimes q)$, and its composite with the collapse in step 6 is exactly $h_n$. Therefore it is invertible. Its inverse $V_n\to U_n$ represents the displayed isomorphism in $D(S_n')$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), quotient balancing using the stated common quotient hypotheses

proof.text: For any chain map $P\to\widetilde P$, every formula above takes $s\otimes q$ to the same expression with the image of $q$; hence all comparison squares commute. The pullback and scalar-extension quasi-isomorphism assertions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and exact restriction show that these diagrams also commute after inversion of quasi-isomorphisms. The equivalence $W_B^{-1}\mathcal P_B\simeq D(B)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] then proves independence of $P$ and naturality for every derived morphism, including roofs. Both $U_n,V_n$ are complexes of $S_n'$-modules and the formulas are $S_n'$-linear, so this is an isomorphism in $D(S_n')$, rather than merely an isomorphism after forgetting its quotient action.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), localization and naturality of the K-flat computation; Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor)

proof.text: For a quotient transition $t:S_{n+1}'\to S_n'$, the map of underlying $R'$-complexes sends $s\otimes q$ to $t(s)\otimes q$. The reduced insertion followed by this transition sends it to $t(s)\otimes(1\otimes q)$, which is also transition followed by insertion. The collapse and $h_n$ obey the same equality. Quotient units send $q$ to $1\otimes q$; insertion sends this to $1\otimes(1\otimes q)$, whose collapse and $h_n^{-1}$ give $1\otimes q$. Thus the inverse comparisons commute with all quotient transitions and quotient units. These are sheaf-map equalities by pure-tensor extensionality [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus], and hence remain equalities after localization.

For composable $u$ and $v$ with compatible data, use the canonical pullback compositors computed by ordinary pullback on flat-term K-flat complexes [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Such models remain eligible after each pullback by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. The ordinary compositor collapses $b''\otimes(b'\otimes q)$ to $b''v^{-1}(b')\otimes q$. Inserting scalars twice sends $q$ to $1\otimes(1\otimes q)$, which collapses to $1\otimes q$, exactly insertion for the composite. After reduction, both paths multiply the two coefficient sections in the common final quotient and leave $q$ fixed. Equality follows from associativity of coefficient multiplication and pure-tensor extensionality [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. For the identity morphism the canonical unitor collapses $1\otimes q$ to $q$, so the comparison is the identity. Localizing gives the claimed coherence, and taking inverses preserves every commuting square, proving coherence for the displayed inverse isomorphisms too.
